text: We evaluated an evolution-strategy refinement procedure that uses swap-consistency as its fitness signal, with an ES population of 8, transferring supervision from a pythia-410m weak model to a qwen2.5-3b strong model across 4 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.66 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.89, while the refined transfer model attained 0.66 accuracy with a standard error of 0.01 — essentially matching the weak supervisor rather than recovering any of the gap to the strong ceiling. The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.01 with a standard error of 0.04, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.38. The method therefore does not recover more of the gap than the baseline; on these numbers it underperforms it, and the PGR estimate itself is within two standard errors of zero. With only 4 seeds, these estimates are imprecise, and no claim of improvement over the baseline is supported by the data.
